create.name: Brother Phap Huu
create.bio:
Brother Phap Huu is a Zen Buddhist monk in the Plum Village tradition founded by Thich Nhat Hanh, and has been abbot of Upper Hamlet, the monks' hamlet of Plum Village in the countryside of south-west France, since 2011. He grew up in Canada and first came to Plum Village in 1996, aged nine, travelling with his father and sister. Drawn to the life of the monks, he asked to ordain and became a novice at thirteen in 2002, took full ordination in 2006 and was given the lamp transmission in 2009, which made him a Dharma teacher. For many years he was one of Thich Nhat Hanh's close attendants.

His teaching stays close to daily life: walking meditation, returning to the breath, caring for strong emotions, and building a community in which people hold each other up. He gives Dharma talks and joins question-and-answer panels during the community's retreats, many of which are filmed and shared freely online, and he is known as a warm, practical facilitator with a gift for mentoring younger monastics. With the journalist and leadership coach Jo Confino he co-hosts The Way Out Is In, a long-running podcast on the Zen art of living, and the two have written two short books in the Zen Ways series, Being with Busyness and Calm in the Storm.

free_resources.title: The Way Out Is In: The Zen Art of Living (podcast)
free_resources.description: A long-running podcast, now past a hundred episodes, in which he and Jo Confino talk through Thich Nhat Hanh's teachings and how they apply to ordinary life, often with guests. Free to stream on the Plum Village website and podcast apps.

free_resources.title: In the Footsteps of the Buddha (1/6): The Buddha Down to Earth
free_resources.description: The first of six podcast episodes recorded on a pilgrimage to the places of the Buddha's life in India in early 2026, with the pilgrimage leader Shantum Seth. This one, made in Varanasi, looks at the Buddha as a human being and at impermanence as a daily practice.
